How to lower your customer acquisition cost (CAC) with paid social

Lower CAC rarely comes from one magic audience. It comes from fixing the whole chain between the ad and the paying customer, one lever at a time.

Published November 12, 20265 min read

In this article

  1. First, measure the right CAC
  2. Lever 1: give the algorithm the right signal
  3. Lever 2: creative is the new targeting
  4. Lever 3: shorten the path to purchase
  5. Lever 4: respond in minutes, not hours
  6. Lever 5: budget in steps, by unit economics
  7. A simple CAC review checklist
  8. Where a nearshore team helps
  9. The bottom line
  10. Frequently asked questions
SeePaid media

Quick answer

To lower CAC with paid social, measure cost per paying customer instead of cost per click, feed the platform the right conversion signal, refresh creative constantly (AI UGC makes this affordable), respond to leads within minutes, and scale budget in steps. Most CAC gains come from creative and conversion speed, not from targeting tweaks.

Customer acquisition cost (CAC) is the number that decides whether paid social is an engine or a leak. When it creeps up, the usual reflex is to tweak audiences or switch platforms. In our experience, the bigger and more durable wins sit elsewhere: in what you measure, the creative you run and what happens after the click.

This guide walks through the levers in the order we work them for brands.

First, measure the right CAC

CAC is total acquisition spend divided by new paying customers in the same period. If you spent $10,000 and won 100 new customers, your CAC is $100.

Two common traps hide the real number:

  • Optimizing for proxies. Clicks, CTR and cost per lead are useful diagnostics, but a cheap lead that never buys is expensive.
  • Not connecting sales to ads. If your CRM or checkout does not record which campaign brought each customer, CAC is a guess.

Set a maximum CAC before you touch the campaigns. As a worked example with round numbers: if your average order is $120, gross margin is 50% and a customer buys twice a year, they generate $120 of gross profit annually. If you are willing to invest up to half of that to win them, your maximum CAC is $60. Everything below is about getting comfortably under that line.

Lever 1: give the algorithm the right signal

Meta and TikTok optimize toward whatever event you tell them to. If you optimize for clicks, you get clickers. If you optimize for purchases or qualified leads, you get closer to buyers.

  • Install server-side tracking (Meta's Conversions API, TikTok Events API) alongside the pixel so conversions are not lost to browsers and privacy settings.
  • Optimize for the deepest event that still gets enough volume. A purchase is ideal; a qualified lead or booked call is a good substitute when purchases are rare.
  • Send offline conversions back from your CRM when sales close outside the website.

This is the cheapest CAC lever because it improves every dollar you already spend.

Lever 2: creative is the new targeting

With broad audiences and automated placements, the ad itself does most of the targeting. The hook decides who stops scrolling, and the message decides who clicks with intent.

  • Test many hooks, not many audiences. Change the first three seconds, the opening line and the offer framing.
  • Use creator-style video (UGC) next to polished brand assets. Native-looking content often earns cheaper attention.
  • Refresh before fatigue. When frequency rises and CTR drops, CAC follows.

Producing that volume used to be the bottleneck. AI video changes the math: our AI Filmmaker team produces UGC with avatars, commercials and product shots without sets or shoots. With a fintech operating in Guatemala, Costa Rica and Mexico, CAC was 16% lower with AI UGC than with the other creatives, and CTR was 3.2× higher with a 46% lower cost per click versus the six previous months.

Lever 3: shorten the path to purchase

Every extra step between the ad and the sale costs money.

  • Match the landing page to the ad: same promise, same visual, same offer.
  • Make the page fast on mobile; most paid social traffic is phone traffic.
  • Remove form fields you do not use.
  • For high-consideration products, consider sending people to a conversation (Messenger, Instagram DM or WhatsApp) instead of a long form.

Lever 4: respond in minutes, not hours

For lead-based businesses, speed to lead is often the single biggest CAC lever. Interest fades fast; a lead contacted the next day has often already talked to a competitor.

A chatbot or automated flow can answer instantly, ask qualifying questions, book a call and push the lead into your CRM with its campaign source. That is what our automation work does: it turns paid conversations into customers instead of unanswered messages.

Lever 5: budget in steps, by unit economics

  • Scale budgets gradually so campaigns keep their learning instead of resetting.
  • Shift spend toward the campaigns, products and markets with the lowest measured CAC.
  • Cut what does not reach your maximum CAC after a fair test, even if it "looks good" on reach.

For reference, in our paid social campaigns across Latin America, we typically see lower costs per conversation and per thousand impressions than in our US campaigns, which is one reason some brands test Spanish-speaking markets or US Hispanic audiences in parallel. Results vary by industry, ticket size and country, so treat any range as orientation and validate with your own numbers.

A simple CAC review checklist

QuestionIf the answer is no
Do we know CAC by campaign and by product?Fix tracking and CRM attribution first
Are we optimizing for purchases or qualified leads?Change the optimization event
Did we launch new creative in the last two weeks?Produce new hooks and formats
Do leads get a response within minutes?Automate the first response
Is spend moving toward the lowest-CAC campaigns?Rebalance budget monthly

Frequently asked questions

What is a good CAC?

There is no universal benchmark. A CAC is healthy when it is clearly below the gross profit a customer generates over their lifetime with you. Start from your margin and retention, not from an industry average.

How long does it take to lower CAC?

Measurement and conversion-speed fixes can show results within weeks. Creative testing compounds over months. We plan campaigns to be live within 4 weeks and judge changes on measured CAC, not on the first few days of data.

Does AI UGC actually lower CAC?

It can, mainly because it lets you test many more hooks and formats for the same budget. In our work with a fintech operating in Guatemala, Costa Rica and Mexico, CAC was 16% lower with AI UGC than with the other creatives.

Should I target US Hispanic customers in Spanish?

Test it. Many US Hispanic customers respond to Spanish or bilingual creative, while others prefer English. Run both with the same budget and keep the version with the lower CAC for each product.
